# Ecclesiastes Chapter 9 -- The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** I thought about all this and concluded that the righteous and the wise and everything they do are in God's hands. No one knows whether God will show them favor. Everything that lies ahead is uncertain.

**2** Everyone shares the same fate — the righteous and the wicked, the good and the bad, the religious and the irreligious, those who sacrifice and those who don't. Good people are treated the same as sinners. Those who make promises to God are treated the same as those who are afraid to.

**3** It seems so wrong that everyone under the sun shares the same fate. Already prone to evil, people choose the path of madness, for what does it matter? They all end up among the dead.

**4** But there is hope for those who are still alive. As they say, "It's better to be a live dog than a dead lion!"

**5** The living at least know they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, and even their name is forgotten. **6** Whatever they did in their lives — loving, hating, envying — is all long gone. They no longer play a part in anything here on earth.

**7** So go ahead. Eat your food with joy, and drink your wine with a happy heart, for God approves of this! **8** Wear fine clothes and anoint yourself with fragrance.

**9** Live happily with the woman you love through all the fleeting days of life that God has given you under the sun. The wife you love is your reward for all your earthly toil.

**10** Whatever you do, do well. For when you go to the grave, there will be no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

**11** I have noticed something else under the sun. The fastest runner doesn't always win the race, and the strongest warrior doesn't always win the battle. The wise sometimes go hungry, and the skillful are not necessarily wealthy. And those who are educated don't always get the recognition they deserve. It is all decided by chance, by being in the right place at the right time.

**12** People can never predict when hard times might come. Like fish in a net or birds in a trap, people are caught by sudden tragedy.

**13** Here is another bit of wisdom that has impressed me as I have watched the way our world works. **14** There was a small town with only a few people, and a great king came with his army and besieged it. **15** A poor, wise man knew how to save the town, and so it was rescued. But afterward no one thought to thank him.

**16** So even though wisdom is better than strength, those who are wise will be despised if they are poor. What they say will not be appreciated for long.

**17** Better to hear the quiet words of a wise person than the shouts of a foolish king.

**18** Better to have wisdom than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy a lot of good.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The great "carpe diem" passage (vv.7-10):** This is Qoheleth at his most life-affirming. Eat joyfully, drink happily, love your spouse, work with purpose — because death is final and there's no second chance. This is not hedonism but urgency: life is short and death is permanent, so live fully now.

**Time and chance (v.11):** This verse shatters the meritocratic illusion. Speed doesn't guarantee victory. Strength doesn't ensure winning. Wisdom doesn't bring wealth. We like to think the best person wins, but Qoheleth says outcomes depend on timing and circumstance — factors beyond our control.

**The forgotten wise man (vv.13-16):** This parable illustrates Qoheleth's bittersweet view of wisdom: it works, it saves, but it is not rewarded. The poor wise man is the hero of the story and its victim.

*-- PNEUMA*
